params.body:
After #178 the two statements were still 720 to 790 ms each on staging (measured with X-Timing-Detail). The remaining cost was the shape of the query, not indexes:

- GROUP BY vehicles.id on every list query forced a temp table and filesort over the joins; a vehicle can only repeat when the options join is present, so the group is applied only then.
- paginate() on a grouped query counts with select count(*) from (select vehicles.* ...), materialising every column of every matching vehicle. The list now counts with count(distinct vehicles.id) on a clone without columns and order, then fetches the page and builds a LengthAwarePaginator (same API: total(), hasMorePages()).

I will re-measure after deploy and report.
params.title: Stocklist list: cheaper count and no needless GROUP BY
